title: ‘Zoomsday’ hack uncovered using fewer than 20 AI prompts
slides: How did 20 AI prompts bypass Zoom security?
Attackers exploited hidden image metadata in calls.
The hack needed zero victim interaction—just one lured click.
Your Zoom version is likely vulnerable today.
Update immediately, then audit your meeting logs.
thread_text:
1. One click, zero interaction

A single lure click on a malicious link was enough. No user action beyond that was required.

2. Hiding in plain sight

Attackers embedded the exploit in image metadata within Zoom calls, making it invisible to standard security scans.

3. Your version is exposed

Most current Zoom builds are vulnerable. The attack doesn't need a victim to do anything but open a call.

4. The silent breach

The hack goes unnoticed, leaving no trace in usual logs. That's why auditing is critical.

5. Update now, audit later

Check your Zoom version today and update. Then review meeting logs for unusual activity—do it this week.

Your Zoom app could let an attacker in with just one click on a lure—and you'd never notice a thing. 🎯

If you host meetings or share screens for work, that's your entry point. Check your Zoom version and update today. Then audit your meeting logs for odd activity this week. 🔍
